findings.evidence: The declaration assumes principal-value existence on every adjacent interval `t k` to `t (k + 1)` and concludes existence on `t 0` to `t n`; `forall_lt` identifies only the bounded-quantifier syntax and not the adjacent-interval condition.
findings.fix: Rename it to describe finite-partition concatenation, such as `cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_partition` or a name aligned with `hasCauchyPVAt_inv_sub_sum_range`.
findings.issue: `cauchyPVExistsAt_inv_sub_of_forall_lt` uses the proof-shaped and semantically incomplete suffix `of_forall_lt`; the naming convention requires descriptive names and permits hypotheses after `of` only when their mathematical content is conveyed.

summary: One theorem name encodes the syntactic shape of its hypothesis instead of the finite-partition property, making the API difficult to discover.
